title: Odd Lots: What Happens When Billionaires Turn to Politics
summary:
What happens when simply getting rich is not enough and billionaires continue to strive for something greater?

Stanford Professor Francis Fukuyama joins Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal on the Odd Lots podcast to discuss what drives the richest and most powerful people in the world and what happens when their ambitions get entangled with politics. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Treasuries Gain as Growing Confidence in Warsh Calms Market
summary: US Treasuries rose as oil price declines and gains for UK government bonds reinforced improving sentiment after the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate hike and pledge to throttle inflation.

title: Stanford Professor Fukuyama on Today’s Extremist Ideology
summary:
Francis Fukuyama's 1989 essay “The End of History?” argued that liberal democracy would not only defeat communism, but that its partisans might miss the “courage, imagination and idealism” that defined the ideological battle.

The Stanford professor joins Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal on the Odd Lots podcast to discuss how his argument has evolved since the end of the Cold War and what's driving today's extremist ideology. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Lazard's Van Nostrand Says Markets Are Entering a Supply-Side Era
summary: Lazard Asset Management CIO Eric Van Nostrand says recent volatility in geopolitics, oil prices and higher rates reinforces Lazard’s view that markets are shifting into a new supply-side era, where outcomes are being driven more by supply shocks than by consumer demand. He speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Inflation Pressures Remain in 'Cyclical Upswing,' Says Lakshman Achuthan
summary:
US Treasuries advanced Thursday as the Federal Reserve’s interest rate hike reassured investors that the central bank is determined to tame inflation. 
Lakshman Achuthan, COO and co-founder at ECRI, reacts to the Fed decision and what comes after the first hike of a rate hike cycle. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Mozambique, Senegal Eurobonds Top Emerging Market Returns, Lifted by IMF Talks
summary: Mozambique and Senegal’s eurobonds are topping returns across emerging markets, spurred by progress in talks with the International Monetary Fund over new programs.

title: US Stocks Rebound From Fed Decision Day Slump as Oil Falls
summary: US stocks rose at the open following the Federal Reserve’s first interest-rate increase since 2023 as oil prices fell for a second day in a row and Treasury yields edged lower.

title: Generac Up on Amazon Agreement; Coreweave Kicks Off Fundraising | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Generac (GNRC) shares are jumping after the company and Amazon execute a long-term supply agreement, with initial deliveries of backup generators expected to total $2.4b in 2027, 2028.
- CoreWeave (CRWV) is the most actively traded stock in the premarket as it kicked off a fresh round of fundraising that includes a $3 billion convertible bond issue and a vehicle for potential share sales.
- Lockheed Martin (LMT) shares are moving on news the Pentagon and Lockheed Martin have struck a framework agreement for a multi-year production contract for the Joint Advanced Tactical Missile, or JATM. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: BOE's Bailey Says Feed-Through of Energy Shock Has Been 'Subdued'
summary: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey discusses the impact of higher energy costs on the UK and the feed-through effect on wider inflation. He speaks after policymakers opted to hold interest rates at 3.75%. "So far that feed-through has been quite subdued," Bailey says. "But it is early days." (Source: Pool)

title: Tata Sons to List, Tata Trusts Calls Chair Chandrasekaran's Extension ‘Illegal’
summary: Tata Sons Pvt. said it would pursue a stock listing and give its chairman another five-year term despite strong — and public — opposition from the founding-family patriarch, setting up a showdown at one of India’s oldest conglomerates.

title: US Stocks (SPY) Poised to Turn a Corner, Citadel Securities’ Rubner Says
summary: Citadel Securities’ Scott Rubner is growing “increasingly constructive on what comes next” as US equities head into the final quarter of the year.

title: Aramco Hunts for Fuel Supply in the Mediterranean After Attacks
summary: Oil giant Saudi Aramco has been looking to secure thousands of tons of diesel in the Mediterranean after a series of attacks on its energy facilities over the past few weeks.

title: US Housing Starts Drop Unexpectedly on Multifamily Projects
summary: New US residential construction declined unexpectedly in August to one of the weakest paces since the pandemic, reflecting a plunge in starts of multifamily projects.

title: Gold Surges Along With US Treasuries as Oil Price Slide Deepens
summary: Gold rallied alongside Treasuries as a slump in oil prices helped ease concerns about inflation, following the Federal Reserve’s first interest-rate hike since 2023.

title: Bill Dudley Calls Fed’s 25-Basis-Point Hike ‘Too Small’
summary: Bill Dudley, former New York Fed President and Bloomberg Opinion columnist, says another interest-rate hike from the Federal Reserve is in order “unless the data changes pretty dramatically.” His opinions are his own. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stocks, Treasuries Rally on Optimism Around Fed Inflation Fight
summary:
US stocks rallied alongside Treasuries as falling oil prices lent support to optimism that inflation can be kept under control a day after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates and signaled more tightening to come.
Savita Subramanian, Head: US Equity & Quantitative Strategy at Bank of America, discusses raising her already low S&P 500 year end target. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Jobless Claims Fall to Lowest Level Since July at 196,000
summary: Applications for US unemployment benefits decreased by 10,000 to 196,000 in the week ended Sep. 12, according to Labor Department data released Thursday. Claims fell last week to the lowest level since July, adding to signals of labor market stability. Michael McKee reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Risk of Midterm ‘Blue Wave’ Leaves Defense Stocks Out of Favor
summary: After two years of breakneck gains, shares of military contractors have hit a wall this year. Traders are expecting the pain to deepen further as they position for protracted negotiations and funding delays should Democrats take control of one or both houses of Congress following the midterm elections.
